coverage.summary: Checks, saves, a full multiclass character sheet, spell slots, hit dice, class resources, conditions, rests, and 5e combat against the SRD monsters: attacks against Armor Class, saves, concentration, death saves, grapples and shoves, Shield, Counterspell and Parry, Haste and Slow, spells that change the numbers, exhaustion, and a board in feet with cover and height.

naturals.$comment: 2014 rules: a natural 20 or 1 decides attack rolls only. Checks and saves are pure arithmetic, unlike Marinara's own rules.

migrations.$comment: Layout 10 has cantrips prepared, since they are always ready (0.438.0), so the Game Master's sheet summary lists them. A layout-9 sheet's level-0 spell rows are marked prepared.
Layout 9 counts Relentless Rage's and Overchannel's uses rather than spending them (Capability API 1.801, 0.427.0). A layout-8 sheet's rows of them are marked as counts.
Layout 8 names the Dragonborn's ancestry row Draconic Ancestry, as the table and the trait share one row (0.422.0). A layout-7 sheet's row stored under the doubled name takes the single one.

Layout 7 keeps Pact of the Chain's own Find Familiar prepared, as the pact's spell is always known, so a fight's setup can call its imp, quasit, pseudodragon or sprite (0.421.0). A layout-6 sheet's row of it is ticked; the plain Find Familiar row, which a wizard may hold unprepared, is left as it is.

Layout 6 names the Way of the Open Hand's prone pick for its effect, beside its Push and No Reactions picks (0.419.0). A row stored on layout 5 under the old name takes the new one; the catalog id is unchanged.

Layout 5 reads a finesse weapon's attack row as the better of Strength and Dexterity (1.793). A row stored on layout 4 for one of the SRD's six finesse weapons, holding Strength or Dexterity, now reads finesse, which is never worse than either.

Layout 4 has a level for each class in place of one level, and hit dice kept per die. A sheet stored on layout 3 reads its level on the class its Class text names (one class named, or the Other class level when the text names none or several, as "Fighter 3 / Wizard 2" does: one number cannot be split between them without asking), and its spent hit dice on the die that class has.

skills.$comment: SRD 5.1, Rogue: thieves' tools, which Expertise may double: "choose two of your skill proficiencies, or one of your skill proficiencies and your proficiency with thieves' tools". A tool, not a skill: every choice of skills of your choice leaves it out (0.402.0).
skills.label: Thieves' tools

fields.$comment: Levels in a class the SRD does not have. They count toward the character level and the Other class hit dice, and nothing else: no class table, resource or spell slot reads them, so a homebrew caster types its slots by hand.
fields.label: Other class

fields.$comment: What the player calls their classes, "Fighter 3 / Wizard 2". The class levels are what the numbers read; this is what the Game Master reads, and the catalogs open on it when it is one class's name ("Wizard"), on any class otherwise.
fields.label: Class

fields.$comment: The class the character began as, which the builder's Class step sets: SRD 5.1 Multiclassing asks for its ability minimum too before a second class.
fields.label: First class

fields.$comment: The class taken second, which its pick in the builder's Class step sets: a third class needs its ability minimum too.
fields.label: Second class

fields.$comment: The subrace the guided builder's Subrace step picked (0.397.0): High Elf, Lightfoot, Red dragon ancestry.
fields.label: Subrace

fields.$comment: A ranger's Favored Enemy choice (1.429): creature types or tags, comma-separated, read by Foe Slayer.
fields.label: Favored enemies (ranger)

fields.$comment: A ranger's Natural Explorer choice: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp or the Underdark, for the Game Master, offered as chips (1.796).
fields.label: Favored terrain (ranger)

fields.$comment: A Draconic Bloodline sorcerer's Dragon Ancestor, as the damage type its table gives (1.429), read by Elemental Affinity.
fields.label: Draconic ancestry damage type (sorcerer)

fields.$comment: Armor Class is worked out from what the character wears (armor_class, below). This is what the player types for an Armor Class that comes from neither armor nor Unarmored Defense, such as Mage Armor's 13 + Dexterity or a natural armor, and the sheet takes whichever is highest; it is the field every character before the items block typed their Armor Class into, so no character's Armor Class drops.
fields.label: Other Armor Class (Mage Armor, natural)

fields.$comment: SRD 5.1, Barbarian Unarmored Defense: "While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit." Monk: the same with Wisdom, "while you are wearing no armor and not wielding a shield". Mage Armor: "the target's base AC becomes 13 + its Dexterity modifier", and the Draconic Bloodline's Draconic Resilience the same "when you aren't wearing armor". A shield and a worn bonus add to any of them but the Monk's.
fields.label: Armor Class without armor

fields.$comment: Which weapons the character adds the proficiency bonus to the attack roll of, when a weapon is held from the bag. SRD 5.1 classes name these: simple and martial weapons (Barbarian, Fighter, Paladin, Ranger); simple weapons and hand crossbows, longswords, rapiers and shortswords (Bard, Rogue); simple weapons (Cleric, Warlock); simple weapons and shortswords (Monk). The Druid's, Sorcerer's and Wizard's short lists of simple weapons, the Monk's shortswords and a people's weapon training are read as the nearest of these. A row on the attack list keeps its own Proficient box.
fields.label: Weapon proficiency

valueLabels.simple_named: Simple weapons, hand crossbows, longswords, rapiers, shortswords

fields.$comment: SRD 5.1, Speed: "Your speed defines how far you can move when you move on your turn." The walking speed for a character with no race picked from the Races catalog, typed by hand (30 is what most SRD races walk). With a race picked, its Speed row's column is the walking speed instead. A fight reads Speed (speed_total).
fields.label: Speed (ft) without a race picked

fields.$comment: Feet added to the walking speed, whatever gives it: a Monk's Unarmored Movement, a feat, a homebrew race.
fields.label: Speed bonus (ft)

fields.$comment: SRD 5.1, Speed: a creature may have "additional movement modes". Typed by hand while something grants a flying speed: the Fly spell (60 feet), Winged Boots or a Broom of Flying. 0 is not flying. On a board a flier crosses water and drops, and rises a level for every 5 feet of it.
fields.label: Fly speed (ft)

fields.$comment: Typed by hand while something grants a swimming speed: a Ring of Swimming (40 feet), a Cloak of the Manta Ray (60), Alter Self's Aquatic Adaptation (the walking speed). 0 is swimming as everybody does, which a fight does not count.
fields.label: Swim speed (ft)

fields.$comment: Typed by hand while something grants a climbing speed: Spider Climb (the walking speed). 0 is climbing as everybody does, which a fight does not count. On a board a climber takes a step of any height.
fields.label: Climb speed (ft)

fields.$comment: SRD 5.1, Size: the character's size category by number, 1 Tiny to 6 Gargantuan. A race picked in the builder sets it (Small 2 for gnomes and halflings, Medium 3 for the rest). A grapple or a shove reads it: neither works on a target more than one size larger.
fields.label: Size (1 Tiny, 2 Small, 3 Medium, 4 Large)

fields.$comment: Strikes one Attack action buys, typed by hand: a floor under the number the class levels give (attacks_per_action_total), for a feature the SRD classes do not have. Characters who typed their Extra Attack here keep it.
fields.label: Attacks per Attack action by hand

fields.$comment: Typed hit points: the By hand method's number, and the Auto method's where it is above 0. A character made before 0.21.0 keeps its number here.
fields.label: Hit point maximum by hand

fields.$comment: SRD 5.1, Hit Points at Higher Levels: "roll the die" or take "the fixed value shown in your class entry". Auto, the default, is the fixed values unless a number is typed by hand, so a character made before 0.21.0 keeps the number it had.
fields.label: Hit points

valueLabels.rolled: Rolled (a hit die for each level after 1st)

fields.$comment: SRD 5.1, Multiclassing, Hit Points and Hit Dice: "You gain the 1st-level hit points for a class only when you are a 1st-level character." The sheet does not know which class came first, so it takes the largest hit die among your class levels unless this names the first class's die.
fields.label: 1st level hit die

valueLabels.d8: d8 (bard, cleric, druid, monk, rogue, warlock)

fields.$comment: The hit die of the Other class level. Every SRD class's die comes from its own level.
fields.label: Other class hit die

fields.$comment: SRD 5.1, High Elf (Cantrip) and Tiefling (Infernal Legacy): a race's own spells are cast with Intelligence or Charisma whatever the class casts with. Set by picking the race in the guided builder.
fields.label: Racial spells ability

fields.$comment: SRD 5.1, Spellcasting: "Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier". Anything else that adds to it goes here: a magic item that improves spell attacks, or a monster whose printed spell attack follows its challenge rating rather than its caster level.
fields.label: Spell attack: other bonus

fields.$comment: SRD 5.1, Spellcasting: "Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier". Anything else that adds to it goes here, for the same reasons as the spell attack's.
fields.label: Spell save DC: other bonus

gmReference: Rulings the Engine leaves to you (SRD 5.1). Surprise: when a fight starts with one side unaware of the other, mark the unaware ones surprised in the encounter. A creature with False Appearance that stayed motionless is indistinguishable from an ordinary object, so a party that did not already know it was there is surprised. Poisons: a contact poison is smeared on an object and affects the first creature that touches it with bare skin; an ingested poison must be swallowed whole, in food or drink. Out of a fight, ask the target for the poison's Constitution save and record what it does with the sheet command. A partial dose may give advantage on the save or deal only half damage on a failure. Midnight tears: no effect until the stroke of midnight, which comes as you pass the day with the sheet command; neutralized before then, it does nothing. Pale tincture: its daily saves are made as you pass each day with the sheet command. Gloves of Swimming and Climbing: an Athletics check to climb or swim says so in the check tag, for="climb" or for="swim", so the gloves' +5 counts. Manacles bind a Small or Medium creature: escaping takes a DC 20 Dexterity check, breaking them a DC 20 Strength check, and without the key a creature proficient with thieves' tools picks the lock with a DC 15 Dexterity check. They have 15 hit points. Contingency: its caster wears a Contingency statuette (when downed, or when harmed); when they cast Contingency, store its contingent spell, one of 5th level or lower with a casting time of one action that can target the caster, in that statuette with standing's into before the fight, and it is cast on them by itself at that moment. Only one contingency at a time: casting it again ends the other. Ring of Telekinesis: telekinesis at will, but only on objects nobody wears or carries. Feather tokens, each an action and gone once used: Anchor, touched to a boat or ship, keeps it from being moved by any means for 24 hours (touching it again ends that); Fan, tossed up on a ship, fills its sails, +5 miles per hour for 8 hours; Swan Boat, touched to water at least 60 feet across, becomes a self-propelled boat 50 feet long that moves 6 miles per hour, carries thirty-two Medium creatures (a Large one counts as four, a Huge one nine) and lasts 24 hours; Tree, touched to open ground outdoors, becomes a nonmagical oak 60 feet tall with a 5-foot trunk and branches spreading 20 feet. Wish, beyond the uses on its menu (each of which puts its stress on the caster): an object of up to 25,000 gp that is not a magic item, no more than 300 feet in any dimension, appears in an unoccupied space the caster can see on the ground; a single recent event is undone by forcing a reroll of any roll made within the last round, with advantage or disadvantage if the caster likes, the caster choosing the reroll or the original (rule what follows); anything greater is the Game Master's to grant, partly grant or twist. Each of these puts the same stress on the caster: tag the Wish stress conditions on their sheet.

gm.checkGuidance: This game uses 5e rules from SRD 5.1. Call for an ability check, skill check or saving throw only when the outcome is uncertain and failure is interesting. Name the skill or the save and set a DC from the ladder below. Never add modifiers, never state a total and never decide the result: the Engine applies the character sheet and reports the outcome. A natural 20 or natural 1 has no special effect on checks or saves.
gm.sheetGuidance: The character sheets below are authoritative. A character can only cast a spell that is on their sheet and only with a slot they still have. When a character spends or regains a resource, takes damage, heals, gains or loses a condition, or rests, record it with the sheet command. If a command is refused, the fiction did not happen: narrate around it. When a Simulacrum is finished, add its duplicate with the party change command, copy_of the beast or humanoid it copies and condition simulacrum: it has half that one's hit point maximum and none of its items. When Raise Dead or Resurrection returns a character to life, set their Back from the dead track to 4.

layers.$comment: Low magic (1.0.2, Capability API 1.813): flavour plus caps. Spells and spell scrolls stop at 5th level; every magic item stays in the game but no seller has one among their wares, the magic dealer and the scribe are gone, and treasure drops one about a fifth as often. A fence's odd lot is the one shady way to buy one. Slots of 6th level and up stay on the sheet, for casting lower spells with them.

layers.summary: Magic is rare and feared. No spell above 5th level, and magic items are seldom found and never sold in shops.

gm.guidance: Low magic is on. Magic is rare, feared and remarked on: few people ever see a spell cast, casters are scarce and often hidden, and NPCs meet magic with awe, suspicion or fear. Nobody, the party or anyone else, knows or casts a spell above 5th level, and nothing in the world reaches past that. Magic items still exist, rare ones included, but they are seldom found and never sold over a counter: one comes from a ruin, a hoard, an old family, the dead or the black market, and each has a story. Do not invent magic items, and give one only as a deliberate, story-worthy reward. Keep creatures of magic out of random and incidental encounters: aberrations, celestials, constructs, dragons, elementals, fey, fiends, undead, and anything that casts spells. You may still build a fight around one on purpose when the story calls for it: give it a reason to exist in a world where magic is rare, and let the party feel how unusual it is.
gm.worldGuidance: Low magic is on. If the player has not said why magic is rare in this world, decide it now and keep to it: what happened (a cataclysm, a purge, a fading source, a law, a curse), when, who remembers it and what it left behind. Build a world where that shows: no schools of wizardry and no magic shops, healing that comes from herbs and hands, a few practitioners who are feared, hunted or prized, and ruins and relics from a time when magic was stronger.

distance.$comment: SRD 5.1, Playing on a Grid: "Each square on the grid represents 5 feet." Every distance in this ruleset is in feet, so one cell is five of them.
distance.label: ft

components.label: Material with a cost, or consumed

ranged.$comment: SRD 5.1, Range: "Your attack has disadvantage when your target is beyond normal range." Ranged Attacks in Close Combat: "You have disadvantage on a ranged attack roll if you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature who can see you and who isn't incapacitated." The Engine reads the second rule from the shooter's own neighbours and cannot ask whether that neighbour sees them.

cover.$comment: SRD 5.1, Cover: "A target with half cover has a +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws. ... A target with three-quarters cover has a +5 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws. ... A target with total cover can't be targeted directly by an attack or a spell." Half cover's obstacle "might be a low wall, a large piece of furniture, a narrow tree trunk, or a creature, whether that creature is an enemy or a friend", so a creature in the way counts. The Engine grades cover by the DMG's corner lines from the attacker; total cover is no line of sight, which no attack or targeted spell gets past. A Dexterity save is helped by cover between the target and where the effect comes from: where a burst lands, else its caster. Woods, ruins and other ground give cover only where they lie between, never from the cell the target stands in (0.379.0, Capability API 1.770). Sacred Flame's save takes no cover, as its text says.

elevation.$comment: SRD 5.1, Falling: "At the end of a fall, a creature takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it fell, to a maximum of 20d6. The creature lands prone, unless it avoids taking damage from the fall." A board level is 5 feet, as wide as a square, so a flier rises a level for every 5 feet of its flight, and one knocked prone or held to a speed of 0 falls as this says unless it hovers. The SRD gives higher ground nothing in an attack, so this says nothing about it; climbing costs and cliffs are the Engine's own.

opportunity.$comment: SRD 5.1, Opportunity Attacks: "You can make an opportunity attack when a hostile creature that you can see moves out of your reach. To make the opportunity attack, you use your reaction." The fight stops and asks whoever may take it, and letting it go by costs nothing.

abilities.$comment: Prepared spells, plus cantrips, which are cast without being prepared and are level 0 on this sheet. What each one does is the catalog entry's own mechanics.

SRD 5.1, Breath Weapon: "The DC for this saving throw equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus." Monk Ki: "Ki save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier." Class selects the feature DC; neither borrows the spellcasting selector.
The warlock's eldritch invocations: one that casts a spell casts it with the warlock's Charisma spell attack and save DC.
The warlock's Pact Boon: Pact of the Blade puts a pact weapon in hand.

conditions.$comment: Only the parts of each condition the Engine can express. Blinded lacks sight and Deafened lacks hearing (Capability API 1.127), so effects that need those senses cannot target them. Charmed joined the list when Capability API 1.29 added an effect for the one thing it does in a fight.

levels.$comment: SRD 5.1, Exhaustion, counted on the sheet track of that name. Every level the track has reached counts, so each adds to the ones below it: "4: Hit point maximum halved", "6: Death". A creature counts it too, and one the SRD makes immune to it names the track among its condition immunities.

SRD 5.1, Raise Dead and Resurrection: "The target takes a -4 penalty to all attack rolls, saving throws, and ability checks. Every time the target finishes a long rest, the penalty is reduced by 1 until it disappears."

checks.$comment: The numbers a contest reads, off the sheet. SRD 5.1 grapples and shoves with Athletics and resists them with Athletics or Acrobatics. A creature without a sheet gives its own, from its printed skills or its ability modifiers.
checks.label: Athletics

readying.$comment: SRD 5.1, Ready: "First, you decide what perceivable circumstance will trigger your reaction. Then, you choose the action you will take in response to that trigger, or you choose to move up to your speed in response to it." "When you ready a spell, you cast it as normal but hold its energy, which you release with your reaction when the trigger occurs ... holding onto the spell's magic requires concentration ... If your concentration is broken, the spell dissipates without taking effect." (1.288)

hiding.$comment: SRD 5.1, Hide: "you make a Dexterity (Stealth) check in an attempt to hide", and "you can't hide from a creature that can see you clearly". Passive Perception: "10 + all modifiers that normally apply to the check", 5 lower while what is seen is only lightly obscured ("disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight", a -5 on a passive score). Search: "you devote your attention to finding something". You give away your position "if you make noise, such as shouting a warning": a verbal component.

poses.$comment: SRD 5.1: an invisible creature is "impossible to see without the aid of magic or a special sense", and Hide in Plain Sight (camouflaged) hides its ranger. Cleric and paladin spells and features are cast praying: the cleric is "a conduit for divine power", the paladin draws "on divine magic through meditation and prayer".

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1, Grappling: replaces one attack of the Attack action, Athletics against the target's Athletics or Acrobatics, and on a win the target is grappled by the grappler. The target can be no more than one size larger.
contests.label: Grapple

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1, Shoving a Creature: the same contest and the same size limit, and the target is knocked prone or pushed 5 feet away.
contests.label: Shove prone

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1, Escaping a Grapple: an action, the escaper's Athletics or Acrobatics against the grappler's Athletics, aimed only at whoever holds on.
contests.label: Escape a grapple

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1: a creature restrained by Web, Entangle, Black Tentacles or a giant spider's web uses its action to make a check against the hold's DC, with the checks the hold names. Only a hold with an escape DC is broken this way, so petrification is not (Capability API 1.175).
contests.label: Break free

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1, Rope of Entanglement: "A target restrained by the rope can use an action to make a DC 15 Strength or Dexterity check (target's choice). On a success, the creature is no longer restrained by the rope" (0.295.0), the rope's own hold.
contests.label: Break free of the rope

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1, Gelatinous Cube: "An engulfed creature can try to escape by taking an action to make a DC 12 Strength check. On a success, the creature escapes and enters a space of its choice within 5 feet of the cube" (Capability API 1.403).
contests.label: Escape the cube

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1, Gelatinous Cube: "A creature within 5 feet of the cube can take an action to pull a creature or object out of the cube. Doing so requires a successful DC 12 Strength check, and the creature making the attempt takes 10 (3d6) acid damage" (Capability API 1.407), the DC and the acid off the engulf.
contests.label: Pull out of the cube

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1, Water Elemental, Whelm: "A creature within 5 feet of the elemental can pull a creature or object out of it by taking an action to make a DC 14 Strength check and succeeding" (Capability API 1.407). Out of it, the grapple ends, and the whelm and its restraint with it.
contests.label: Pull out of the elemental

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1, Stabilizing a Creature: "You can use your action to administer first aid to an unconscious creature and attempt to stabilize it, which requires a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check" (Capability API 1.193), on anybody dying.
contests.label: Stabilize (first aid)

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1, Sword of Wounding: "the wounded creature, or a creature within 5 feet of it, can use an action to make a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check, ending the effect of such wounds on it on a success" (Capability API 1.193).
contests.label: Treat wounds

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1, Grappler: "You can use your action to try to pin a creature grappled by you. To do so, make another grapple check. If you succeed, you and the creature are both restrained until the grapple ends." Offered only to whoever has the feat (0.265.0, Capability API 1.553 and 1.578).
contests.label: Pin (Grappler)

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1, Arcane Hand, Forceful Hand: "The hand attempts to push a creature within 5 feet of it in a direction you choose. Make a check with the hand's Strength contested by the Strength (Athletics) check of the target. If the target is Medium or smaller, you have advantage on the check. If you succeed, the hand pushes the target up to 5 feet plus a number of feet equal to five times your spellcasting ability modifier." Offered only to the hand (0.275.0, Capability API 1.578 and 1.587).
contests.label: Forceful Hand

contests.$comment: SRD 5.1, Arcane Hand, Grasping Hand: "The hand attempts to grapple a Huge or smaller creature within 5 feet of it. You use the hand's Strength score to resolve the grapple. If the target is Medium or smaller, you have advantage on the check." Offered only to the hand (0.280.0, Capability API 1.597); its Crush is the hand's own action.
contests.label: Grasping Hand

sizes.$comment: SRD 5.1, Size Categories. A creature names its own; a character's is the sheet's Size, which a race sets (Small 2, Medium 3).

creatureTypes.$comment: SRD 5.1, Creature Types. A creature names its own and its subtypes a rule reads; every SRD race is humanoid, so a character is.

dying.$comment: Three successes stabilise and three failures kill, which is each track's own maximum. A natural 20 brings the character back up with one hit point and a natural 1 counts twice.

threat.$comment: The scale an opponent NOBODY WROTE is pulled onto. MEASURED from the SRD 5.1 creatures of each challenge rating: health is the lowest to the highest average hit points, defense and toHit are the median Armor Class and the median best attack bonus, damagePerRound is the lowest to the highest best round against one target, and saveDifficulty is the median of the difficulties those creatures' actions name. Damage is measured only from the creatures whose fighting is in their actions, because a spellcaster's printed attack is a dagger and an action this format could not hold is a trait a fight never rolls. A rating the SRD has no creature for, or none that can be measured for damage, takes the midpoint of its nearest neighbours. The caps and floors are then made monotone along the rating order, which is the one place this table is smoothed: a higher rating may never allow less than a lower one, and the numbers themselves are still the SRD creatures' own. This package's own bestiary is never clamped to it.
